sources.entry: LinkAce - Bookmark archive with automatic backups to the Internet Archive, link monitoring, and a full REST API. Installation is done via Docker, or as a simple PHP application. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker/PHP

summary.one_liner: LinkAce is a self-hosted bookmark manager and link archive for organizing, archiving, and sharing saved web links.
summary.what_it_does: LinkAce lets you save links and organize them with lists and tags, with advanced search and filters. It supports multiple users with internal sharing of links, lists, or tags, and links can be private or public. Automated link monitoring reports when links become unavailable or move, and saved sites are archived via the Internet Archive. A full REST API exposes its features to other apps, and a bookmarklet and automatic title/description generation help when saving. Private and public lists are available as RSS feeds, and bookmarks can be imported and exported as HTML. The README also mentions backups of the database and application to AWS S3-compatible storage and OAuth/OIDC SSO login.
use_cases: monitoring links for broken or moved pages
sharing link collections with family or coworkers
organizing research resources with tags and lists
importing and exporting browser bookmarks as HTML
how_to_run: Install with Docker (see the wiki for the full setup guide)
Or install as a simple PHP application without Docker (see the wiki)
Kubernetes setup is available (Beta) per the README
Official managed hosting is available (Beta) per the README
notable: Automated archiving of saved sites via the Internet Archive
Automated link monitoring for unavailable or moved links
Full REST API and Zapier availability
OAuth and OIDC SSO login support
Private or public links and lists with RSS feeds
caveats: Official managed hosting and Kubernetes setup are marked Beta
The author does not offer free personal support; community discussions are the support channel
Detailed setup and configuration are in the external wiki rather than the README
